statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty and a half hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; nineteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress is 59 in the elevated band, one point above the previous hour, after a Houthi media official stated that Bab el-Mandeb will be closed, a strait through which roughly twelve per cent of world trade normally passes, while the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut, WTI sits at $100.05 and the 16 September FOMC is priced near 85.5 per cent for a 25 basis point hike. Confidence is 87: every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only missing evidence class is a live price path that no venue can supply while the market is closed.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in nineteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures failed mean reversion has no path to measure across most of this horizon. Second, the last observable session was orderly and two-way rather than one-way: the cash range spanned only 159.61 points, the close finished about 105 points below the high, nine of eleven sectors rose and VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84. Third, none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail is observed, because observing them requires a live tape. The severity of the macro and geopolitical backdrop is therefore expressed in Stress at 59 rather than in Tail, consistent with the documented separation between a difficult environment and a pathological price path. The one narrow window flagged in this horizon is the 22:00 UTC restart and the two hours that follow it, where conditional Tail reaches the WATCH band on gap and thin-liquidity risk that is anticipated rather than observed.
headline: More than thirty hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while a Houthi media official says Bab el-Mandeb will be closed after the group took Perim island and the full Yemeni Red Sea coast, the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supply off its route, WTI sits at $100.05 after a 20 per cent month and a hot August CPI has left the 16 September FOMC priced near 85.5 per cent for a rate hike.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against the macro backdrop. Exchange documentation confirms the mechanism behind the gap in evidence: CME equity index futures run from Sunday 17:00 to Friday 16:00 Chicago time, which places the halt at 21:00 UTC on Friday and the restart at 22:00 UTC on Sunday. The shared delayed cross-asset context file is 119 minutes old and marked partial this run, so it fails both its freshness and its health gate and is used only as weak background; its content in any case describes the same Friday session.

The backdrop behind Stress is genuinely severe and pulls the other way. Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline on Friday after a drone attack that both Riyadh and Baghdad traced to Iraq; the 1,200-kilometre line had been carrying 4 to 5 million barrels a day, 4 to 5 per cent of global supply, as the main route out for Middle East crude while the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely shut by war. Houthi forces seized Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb after taking Mokha and have now taken full control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, with the internationally recognised government launching air strikes along the west coast in response. The new element this hour is rhetorical rather than physical: the deputy head of the Houthi media office stated on X that Bab el-Mandeb will be closed in response to what he called a Saudi blockade, a strait through which roughly twelve per cent of world trade normally passes. Reporting also notes that the Houthis asked Washington not to intervene and that the Crown Prince has pressed for direct U.S. military action, which Washington has so far declined. Analysts differ on whether a sustained closure is feasible, with one noting that a hint of danger is already enough to move shipping behaviour. WTI settled at $100.05 and Brent at $104.61, down 2.37 and 2.81 per cent on the day after Iranian state media flagged a Gulf-Iran meeting in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, but still about 9.7 per cent higher on the week and 20.15 per cent on the month. That mix of escalating rhetoric against an active de-escalation track is why Stress moves one point to 59 rather than stepping sharply.

The rate channel is the second Stress input. August CPI, released on 11 September, rose 0.4 per cent on the month against 0.1 per cent in July and 3.4 per cent over twelve months, while core rose 0.3 per cent on the month against 0.2 per cent in July and 2.4 per cent over the year. The energy index rose 2.1 per cent on the month and 16.3 per cent on the year, with gasoline up 3.9 per cent on the month and 27.4 per cent on the year and accounting for over a third of the monthly all-items increase, which is the channel through which the supply shock reaches the policy decision. Yields are correspondingly elevated: the 10 September H.15 observation shows the 2-year at 4.56 per cent, the 5-year at 4.75 per cent, the 10-year at 4.95 per cent and the 30-year at 5.37 per cent against a federal funds effective rate of 3.63 per cent. The FOMC meets on 15 and 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections, and futures price roughly 85.5 per cent odds of a 25 basis point increase to 3.75 to 4.00 per cent. One further index-structural item was verified this hour and sits beyond this horizon: the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance lifts the SpaceX weighting materially, with portfolio adjustments at the close on 18 September and new weights effective before the open on 21 September.

Tail nevertheless stays at 6. The documented separation is deliberate: event importance, surprise magnitude, forecast dispersion and generic volatility belong in Stress and Confidence, while Tail requires an observed price path that denies meaningful retracement. For most of this horizon no such path can exist, and the last one that did exist was orderly. The single narrow window worth flagging is the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, where an entire weekend of pipeline, Perim, strait-closure and inflation news meets a book that has not quoted since Friday evening. Conditional Tail reaches 22 there and eases to 21 and 20 across the following two hours, which maps to WATCH and defines the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. That step is anticipatory and is held inside the WATCH band rather than pushed to a blocking level, because a hypothetical gap is not an observed one and a restart that reprices in an orderly two-way fashion would justify a prompt return to the low band.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 03:00 UTC on 12 September to 02:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there for the rest of the window, in normal mode throughout, tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 59 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53 and 56 to 58 by the close of the window as attention turned to the restart and the weekend escalation reports. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 through the middle of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window is a revision: each slot reproduces the value published at that hour.
outlookSummary: Nineteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's twentieth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It steps to 22 in the restart hour, then eases to 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, and falls back to 19 and 18 by the close of the horizon. Those three WATCH slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. Stress dips a point to 58 through the quiet overnight stretch, then builds to a 64 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture and the approaching FOMC, before easing to 60 as Asian pricing is assumed to establish. Confidence declines gently from 87 to 78 at the restart, reflecting the widening gap between the last verified print and the hour being described, then recovers to 81 once a live venue would exist again. Every slot after the first frames structure conditionally: no gap direction, pullback depth or retracement behaviour is claimed as observed, and the 16 September FOMC decision, the Monday Iran-GCC meeting on Hormuz and the 18 to 21 September Nasdaq-100 rebalance flows all sit beyond this horizon.
